claim: Linum published the P-JiT 21K post on November 4, 2026, by Sahil and Manu Chopra.
quote: Training a Text-to-Image Model for $21K

claim: Linum describes itself as a two-person lab training its own video models from scratch.
quote: We're a 2-person research lab training our own generative video models entirely from scratch.

claim: The model is released under Apache 2.0 as a research release.
quote: Research release · Apache 2.0

claim: Linum reports a total compute cost of $21,038 across 8,415 H100-hours, priced at $2.50 per H100-hour (company-reported).
quote: 8,415 H100-hours pretraining on 64 H100s, restarts included priced at $2.50 per H100-hour

claim: Pretraining cost $20,348 (8,139 H100-hours); post-training cost $690 (276 H100-hours), per Linum.
quote: Pretraining $ 20,348 8,139 H100-hours × $2.50 610M samples at 512², then 50M at 1024² Post-training $ 690 276 H100-hours × $2.50

claim: Linum says the run is a proof of concept toward its next video model, not the end product.
quote: For us, this $21K training run is a proof-of-concept along the way to our next video model.

claim: P-JiT uses 32x32 token reduction versus the 16x16 common in models like FLUX-2, which Linum says gives a 4x smaller attention context (company-reported).
quote: Linum v2 used a 16×16 token reduction like most models (e.g. FLUX-2). P-JiT enables 32×32 token reduction. This implies a 4× reduction in attention context-window.

claim: Linum says P-JiT converges in 11x fewer samples than its previous model Linum v2 (company-reported, vs own baseline).
quote: It's a pixel-space model that converges in 11× fewer samples than Linum v2 with 4× more aggressive token reduction

claim: The 11x figure is 11.3x fewer training samples to reach Linum v2's FD-DINOv2 score, measured on the earlier P-JiT checkpoint.
quote: It reaches Linum v2's FD-DINOv2 on 11.3× fewer training samples.

claim: On the earlier P-JiT checkpoint, Linum's own prompt-following benchmarks favored its older Linum v2 model.
quote: Surprisingly, Linum v2 beats pixel-space models in prompt-following benchmarks

claim: Linum v2 scored 0.80 on GenEval counting vs 0.56 for P-JiT (earlier checkpoint).
quote: It turns out Linum v2 scores 0.80 on counting (e.g., getting exactly three apples in an image) while P-JiT scores 0.56

claim: The model has 2.18B parameters at sampling; training-only heads add about 0.24B.
quote: 2.18B params at sampling · purple heads are training-only and add ~0.24B, for ~2.42B in training

claim: The text encoder is a frozen Qwen3.5-4B model.
quote: The text representation comes from a frozen Qwen3.5-4B model, which we read at layers 7, 15 and 27

claim: Pretraining ran on 64 H100 GPUs across 8 nodes.
quote: 64× H100 (8 nodes) · bf16 · FSDP2 · 32 images per GPU

claim: Post-training used a variant of Finite Difference Flow Optimization (FDFO) with JEV-Image and human judges.
quote: For post-training, we used a variant of Finite Difference Flow Optimization (FDFO) with JEV-Image and human-in-the-loop judges.

claim: The model cannot render text because text-heavy images were deliberately filtered out.
quote: This model was not trained with images of rendered text (no infographics, PDFs, pages of books, PowerPoint slides), so it cannot write text or generate posters.

claim: Linum says the model struggles with full bodies, many entities, multi-person interactions and world knowledge.
quote: there are a few areas where the model struggles: full body, many entities (e.g. 6 cars, crowds), multi-person interactions, and world knowledge.

claim: Linum suggests a larger (e.g. 7B) model and more post-training would likely help.
quote: Training a larger model (e.g. 7B parameters) and further post-training would likely mitigate these issues.

claim: Linum calls it an experimental research artifact, not a production model.
quote: Research checkpoint: this is an experimental research artifact, not a production model.

claim: Short prompts give worse images; by default the code rewrites prompts using Claude Opus 5.5 via OpenRouter, requiring an API key.
quote: short prompts give noticeably worse images. So by default `generate.py` first rewrites your prompt into a caption of that kind with Claude Opus 5.5 through [OpenRouter](https://openrouter.ai), which needs an OpenRouter API key

claim: Running the model needs a CUDA GPU; weights are 8.7 GB fp32 plus an 8 GB text encoder.
quote: The model needs a CUDA GPU: its weights are 8.7 GB in fp32 and the text encoder 8 GB in bf16,

claim: The GitHub repo and model card were written by Claude Opus 5.5 from Linum's internal repo, per Linum.
quote: The Huggingface Model Card and Github Repo were written automatically by Claude Opus 5.5.

claim: Linum's data pipeline filtered tens of billions of images and videos; sources are not named.
quote: We need to filter down tens of billions of images and videos to create our pre-training dataset.

claim: Linum is aiming for a 10x improvement in speed and cost for its next video model, Linum v3.
quote: So, we're aiming for a 10× improvement in speed and cost for our next model.

claim: The founder's Show HN post describes the run as ~$20K on 660M samples, released as Apache 2.0 open weights.
quote: Specifically, we trained it for ~$20K on 660M samples.

claim: HN commenters asked where the training data came from.
quote: What open source datasets did you use? Or did you pirate like the big labs ?

claim: An HN commenter questioned how much cherry-picking went into the showcase gallery.
quote: Looking at the failures, I wonder how much cherry picking went into the showcase.

claim: An HN commenter said the model shows typical text-to-image flaws: over-smoothing, shine, mangled limbs.
quote: Over smoothing, lots of uncanney shine, mangled limbs and such.

claim: An HN commenter noted almost every hand in the samples is wrong.
quote: It looks really good! Except almost every hand is wrong.

claim: JiT (Li & He, 2025) showed large-patch pixel Transformers can be strong generative models without a tokenizer; P-JiT builds on this.
quote: We show that simple, large-patch Transformers on pixels can be strong generative models: using no tokenizer, no pre-training, and no extra loss.

claim: PixArt-alpha (2023) reported a ~$26,000 training cost vs $320,000 for Stable Diffusion v1.5, so low-cost T2I training predates Linum.
Sony's MicroDiT paper (2024) trained a 1.16B text-to-image model for $1,890.
quote: we train a 1.16 billion parameter sparse transformer with only \$1,890 economical cost

claim: FDFO, the post-training method Linum adapted, is a March 2026 arXiv paper.
quote: Finite Difference Flow Optimization for RL Post-Training of Text-to-Image Models
